draft.title: Lewin's force field analysis
card: Kurt Lewin said a business is held in balance by two sets of forces. Driving forces push for change. Restraining forces push against it.
Change happens when the driving forces outweigh the restraining forces. If the restraining forces are stronger, the business stays as it is.
Managers list the forces on each side. They weigh each one and rank it by how strong it is.
Managers then act, usually by strengthening a driving force or weakening a restraining force. After that they check the result to see if the change worked.
draft.remember: Change happens when driving forces outweigh restraining forces. Weigh, act, then check.

a.q: According to Lewin, when does a business change?
opts: When driving forces outweigh restraining forces
When restraining forces outweigh driving forces
When driving and restraining forces are removed
When managers list the forces on each side
a.why: Lewin said change happens when the forces pushing for it are stronger than the forces pushing against it. If restraining forces are stronger, the business stays as it is. Listing forces is only a step managers take and does not cause change.
a.clue: Think about which side has to be stronger.

b.q: Priya manages a bakery in Geelong. Staff resist a new ordering system, and this is the strongest force against change. What should she do first to use force field analysis well?
opts: Weigh and rank all the forces, then act on the strongest
Install the system and check the result later
Drop the system, as staff resistance ends the matter
Count the forces on each side and follow the longer list
b.why: Lewin's method is to weigh and rank the forces, then act, then check. Strong resistance does not end the matter, as managers can weaken it. Counting forces is not enough, because one strong force can outweigh several weak ones.
b.clue: Strength of a force matters, not just how many there are.

a.best: When driving forces outweigh restraining forces

b.best: Weigh and rank all the forces, then act on the strongest

problems.detail: The question asks what Priya should do 'first', but the right option bundles several steps (weigh, rank, then act). It also says to 'act on the strongest', which the card does not teach. The card says managers act by strengthening a driving force or weakening a restraining force. Consider 'then act to weaken the strongest restraining force' or removing 'first'.

proposal.title: Lewin's force field analysis
card: Kurt Lewin said a business is held in balance by two sets of forces. Driving forces push for change. Restraining forces push against it.
Change happens when the driving forces outweigh the restraining forces. If the restraining forces are stronger, the business stays as it is.
Managers list the forces on each side. They weigh each one and rank it by how strong it is, since one strong force can outweigh several weak ones.

Managers then act, usually by strengthening a driving force or weakening a restraining force, such as training staff to ease their resistance. After that they check the result to see if the change worked.
proposal.remember: Change happens when driving forces outweigh restraining forces. Weigh, act, then check.

a.q: According to Lewin, when does a business change?
opts: When driving forces outweigh restraining forces
When restraining forces outweigh driving forces
When driving and restraining forces are removed
When managers list the forces on each side
a.why: Lewin said change happens when the forces pushing for it are stronger than the forces pushing against it. If restraining forces are stronger, the business stays as it is. Listing forces is only a step managers take and does not cause change.
a.clue: Think about which side has to be stronger.

b.q: Priya manages a bakery in Geelong. She has weighed and ranked the forces, and staff resistance to a new ordering system is the strongest force against it. What should she do next?
opts: Weaken staff resistance, such as by training staff
Drop the system, as the strongest force opposes it
Follow whichever side has the longer list of forces
Wait for the driving forces to grow stronger on their own
b.why: After weighing and ranking, managers act by strengthening a driving force or weakening a restraining force, so Priya can work to ease staff resistance. Dropping the system is tempting, but a strong restraining force can be weakened rather than accepted. Counting forces misses the point, because strength matters more than number.
b.clue: Managers can change how strong a force is.
